questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it gave me the opportunity to practice my french within an academic setting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be difficult to understand the administrative work in a strange university. Spend a lot on time on that!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It is more analog at a french university, so a bit more difficult to figure the system out compared to what I was used to

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The erasmus coordinators at Lille was very welcoming and helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There has been some unclear things regarding my final exams (that I havent been added to the list of students) which made me miss 2 of my finals. That was not good enough

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Residence

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Its was a well equipped room with a kitchenette and bathroom

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a bit far awau from the city (in a quite residential area) so its not very inspiring or entertaining to live in, but the rooms were okay

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Location, not good 
Rooms, very good

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the beginning it was fine

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to find the courses on papers hanging around the different campus' which is quite confusing, but once you understand the system it's alright - a bit oldschool. But then you tell the teacher you'd like to participate in a given cours, and wihtin the month of arrival you send an e-mail of your choosen courses to the erasmus coordinator

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I thought we were kind of on our own regarding finding the cours that we wanted

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was okay easy

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try different courses before settling down on the ones you want. 
Here about the different types of exams in each cours, so you know what to expect

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We had courses ranging from 1st year to 3rd year students. It is (obviously) a bit more difficult to join a cours at its 3rd year if you haven't had courses regarding that subject

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All from group work to teacher talking at the board

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Notion de culture en sciences sociales 
Médias, publics et démocratie 
Documentation et édition 
Atelier d'écriture 
Culture et société 
Lire et écrire les mythes 
Sémiologie d'images fixe 
Introduction à l'analyse des images 
Édition jeunesse 
Francais extensif

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Lire et écrire les mythes and Introduction à l'analyse des images

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is tough going to a new university as the handle things differently 
Try not to spend all of your time on administrative work!! (because there is a lot, and it can be very confusing and overwhelming) 
Expect to be physically more present in school, than you are in CPH!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to find housing in the center of Lille

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The french and the friends I made at the university

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All of the administrative work!
